title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: September 27, 2026 – Training Camps Around the Corner!

items.headline: Stephen Curry Signs Two-Year, $116M Extension with Warriors
items.summary: Golden State Warriors superstar Stephen Curry has reportedly agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension through the 2028-29 season. The deal, which doesn't impact the upcoming 2026-27 season's cap, sees Curry leave approximately $20 million on the table, creating crucial cap flexibility for the Warriors for future moves.

items.headline: Pistons' Jalen Duren Rejects $200M Extension, Considers Qualifying Offer
items.summary: Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren is embroiled in a contract dispute, having rejected a reported five-year, $200 million extension offer. Duren, an All-Star and All-NBA Third Team selection last season, is now considering accepting a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, which would make him an unrestricted free agent next summer.

items.headline: Clippers Hit with Heavy Sanctions for Salary Cap Scandal
items.summary: The NBA has announced severe penalties against the Los Angeles Clippers, stripping the franchise of five first-round draft picks (one each from 2029 to 2033) and imposing a $30 million fine. Owner Steve Ballmer has also been suspended from league and team activities for one year following a salary cap scandal.

items.headline: Hornets Trade Buddy Hield to Bulls for Rob Dillingham
items.summary: The Charlotte Hornets have traded veteran shooting guard Buddy Hield to the Chicago Bulls in exchange for 21-year-old guard Rob Dillingham and cash considerations. This marks Dillingham's third team since February, while Hield, an 11-year veteran, joins his seventh NBA franchise.

items.headline: Kawhi Leonard Traded to Clippers in Blockbuster Deal
items.summary: In a significant offseason move on September 14, Kawhi Leonard was traded to the Los Angeles Clippers. The Toronto Raptors received Gradey Dick, Brandon Ingram, a 2027 first-round pick swap right, and multiple future first and second-round picks in return.

items.headline: Pelicans Acquire Johnson, Gibson from Grizzlies
items.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans completed a trade with the Memphis Grizzlies on September 24, acquiring AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson. In exchange, the Grizzlies received Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, the Raptors' 2031 second-round pick, and a 2032 second-round pick swap.

items.headline: Pistons Explored Trades for Durant, Irving, Leonard
items.summary: The Detroit Pistons reportedly made aggressive attempts this offseason to pair a superstar with Cade Cunningham, targeting high-profile players such as Kevin Durant, Kyrie Irving, and Kawhi Leonard. Insider reports indicate Detroit directly contacted the Houston Rockets about a potential Durant trade.

items.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo Joins Miami Heat in Offseason Blockbuster
items.summary: In one of the most impactful moves of the offseason, two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded from the Milwaukee Bucks to the Miami Heat. He was joined by Bobby Portis, while the Bucks received Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis, the No. 13 pick in the 2026 draft, and multiple future draft picks.

items.headline: LeBron James Signs with Philadelphia 76ers
items.summary: After leaving the Los Angeles Lakers, four-time MVP LeBron James has signed with the Philadelphia 76ers as a free agent, teaming up with new arrival Jaylen Brown for his 24th NBA season.

items.headline: Pelicans Make Multiple Free Agent Signings
items.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans have been active in free agency, signing Bennedict Mathurin to a two-year, $15.375 million deal, DeAndre Jordan to a two-year minimum salary contract, and Trendon Watford to a one-year minimum deal. Other signings include Kobe Bufkin, Caleb Houstan, and Christian Koloko on non-guaranteed Exhibit 9 contracts.

items.headline: Ben Simmons Signs with Sacramento Kings
items.summary: Former All-Star Ben Simmons has signed with the Sacramento Kings, seeking an NBA comeback.

items.headline: Pacers Add Kelly Oubre, Larry Nance, and Braden Smith
items.summary: The Indiana Pacers have bolstered their roster with the additions of Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr., and rookie Braden Smith heading into the 2026-27 season. Oubre signed a two-year, $16.5 million fully guaranteed contract.

items.headline: Lonzo Ball Denies Retirement Rumors, Seeks Opportunity
items.summary: Lonzo Ball has denied recent retirement rumors, stating he is still actively seeking an opportunity to play in the NBA.

items.headline: Three First-Time Head Coaches Highlight NBA's New Era
items.summary: The 2026-27 NBA season will feature three first-time head coaches: Dusty May for the Dallas Mavericks, Micah Nori for the Portland Trail Blazers, and Sean Sweeney for the Orlando Magic. Brian Keefe has also been officially named the Washington Wizards' 26th head coach.

items.headline: Deni Avdija Cracks ESPN's Top 30 Player Rankings
items.summary: Portland Trail Blazers forward Deni Avdija has achieved his highest career ranking on ESPN's latest NBA player list, coming in at No. 27. This marks a significant jump from his No. 66 ranking last year, after he averaged 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 6.7 assists last season. Avdija was not cleared to play for Israel in FIBA World Cup qualifiers due to a complex back injury he dealt with last season.

items.headline: NBA Training Camps Set to Open September 29
items.summary: The unofficial start of the 2026-27 NBA season is just around the corner, with all training camps scheduled to open on Monday, September 29. Teams will begin their preparations for the upcoming regular season, which tips off on October 20.

items.headline: Knicks Defend Title, Brunson's Ranking Sparks Debate
items.summary: The New York Knicks enter the 2026-27 season as the reigning NBA champions, their first title since 1973. Despite winning Finals MVP, NBA Cup MVP, and Eastern Conference Finals MVP, ESPN's analytics guru Dean Oliver has controversially placed Jalen Brunson around the No. 25 player in the league, sparking debate among fans and analysts.
